key_insight: PhySGA combines planning, simulation, and feedback agents to make 3D object assembly more physically grounded and reliable for complex interactions.
clinical_relevance: Although not a clinical method, this work may improve the realism of medical simulation assets, training environments, and robot-assisted virtual procedure planning if adapted to healthcare use cases.
method: Assembly Agent plans global steps and coarse adjustments using geometric and kinematic reasoning.
Critic Agent checks contact dynamics to diagnose simulator states and refine actions in a closed loop.
Action Routers and a self-evolving skill library translate high-level plans into simulator actions and reuse successful trial-and-error strategies.
evidence_signal: In Isaac Sim experiments, the framework reportedly outperforms prior approaches in relation fidelity, physical plausibility, and visual quality.
watch_item: Results are based on simulation benchmarks, so transfer to real-world or clinical environments may require careful validation of robustness and physical fidelity.
paper_title: PhySGA: A Physics-Space Grounded Agentic Framework for Generalizable and Interactive 3D Composition
